title: Fetch–decode–execute
hook: A CPU doesn’t “run a program” in one gulp — it walks the same tiny loop, forever.

steps.caption: Fetch: pull the next instruction from memory into the CPU.

nodeCaptions.mem: Instructions live in memory as ordinary bytes.
nodeCaptions.fetch: The program counter says which address to grab next.

steps.caption: Decode: figure out what that instruction means.

nodeCaptions.decode: The decoder maps the bit pattern to an operation and its operands.

steps.caption: Execute: do the work, then go fetch the next instruction.

nodeCaptions.execute: ALU, registers, memory writes — this is where the effect happens.
nodeCaptions.mem: Then the cycle repeats. Billions of times per second.

takeaways: Programs are streams of instructions the CPU fetches one (or a few) at a time.
Fetch → decode → execute is the loop underneath every language you write.
“Running code” is mostly this cycle, over and over.

quiz.question: What does the CPU do after it executes an instruction?
choices: Shut down until you press a key
Fetch the next instruction and keep going
Wait for the disk to approve it
quiz.explanation: The cycle continues until the program ends, blocks, or the machine stops.
